cause: The complete shared field tuple removed field-name drift, but the orchestrator validator still used dict.get and ordinary Python equality, allowing absent members to become null expectations and allowing integer, float, and boolean values to alias.
prevention: Require explicit presence of every non-claim-path member in the committed response claim and compare projected authority with identical JSON type plus equal value; retain production-shaped regressions for all absent members and integer-float or integer-boolean aliases with indeterminate no-mutation semantics.
summary: A fourth independent review reproduced successful claim-progress acknowledgement when canonical pointer values crossed JSON types or when response-claim members were absent but projected as null, despite the downstream pointer gate rejecting the same authority.
title: Require type-strict complete pointer authority
